items.title: Brent breaks US$100 on Mideast flare-up, fanning inflation fears
items.summary: HONG KONG: Brent broke above US$100 a barrel Wednesday as oil prices surged and stocks struggled on the back of a fresh flare-up in the Middle East crisis, putting upward pressure on inflation ahead of key US data at the end of the week. Tehran also said it would target oil tankers off Kuwait and Bahrain and urged crews to leave their ships, according to the IRNA state news agency. The waterway is an increasingly important route for Saudi oil with the Strait of Hormuz shut.

items.title: UK rejects Israel's 'damaging' sanctions retaliation
items.summary: LONDON: British foreign minister Ed Miliband on Wednesday condemned as "regrettable and damaging" Israel's decision to order the closure of the UK's consulate in Jerusalem as retaliation for London-led Western sanctions over settler violence. "I think they're regrettable and damaging," Miliband told BBC Radio. Miliband rejected suggestions that the sanctions would impact intelligence cooperation with Israel.

items.title: TH: Haj offer letters for 31,600 prospective pilgrims to be issued from Sept 21
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) will begin issuing haj offer letters to 31,600 prospective pilgrims for the 1448H/2027 haj season in stages from Sept 21. "Prospective pilgrims are advised to update their personal information and check their haj turn through THiJARI or at the nearest TH branch," TH said in a statement. For the 1448H/2027 haj season, TH is maintaining the haj cost at RM33,300 per person for Muassah pilgrims for the fourth consecutive year, despite facing inflationary pressures, global economic uncertainties and rising service costs in the Holy Land.

items.title: MACC: Abdul Azeez chose to remain in purple lock-up attire, handcuffs for court appearance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim chose to wear purple police lock-up attire and handcuffs when he appeared in the Sessions Court here today, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said. In a statement, the MACC said its officers, the police escorting Abdul Azeez and his lawyer had advised him to change into ordinary clothes before he was taken to court. However, the MACC said Abdul Azeez insisted on remaining in the lock-up attire and handcuffs until the charge against him had been read.

items.title: Shipping company CEO to be charged tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The chief executive officer of a shipping company will be charged at the Sessions Court here tomorrow. The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission said it had obtained approval to prosecute the individual. "The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has obtained approval to prosecute a chief executive officer of a shipping company," it said in a statement today.

items.title: Court of Appeal overturns RM50,000 defamation award granted to Guan Eng
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today overturned a High Court ruling that had ordered former housing and local government minister Datuk Zuraida Kamaruddin and two others to pay RM50,000 in damages to DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng for defamation. A three-judge panel comprising Justices Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril, Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid, and Datuk Amarjeet Singh unanimously allowed the appeals filed by Zuraida, MalaysiaNow editor Muhammad Abd Ar-Rahman Koya and MNow Media Sdn Bhd. The legal proceedings began on June 7, 2024, when Lim, a former Finance Minister, filed a defamation suit at the Shah Alam High Court, naming Zuraida, Muhammad Abd Ar-Rahman Koya and MNow Media as defendants.

items.title: 7 more Taman Manggis PPR units sealed, residents left scrambling for shelter
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Seven more Taman Manggis People's Housing Project (PPR) units were sealed yesterday, days after Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow defended the sealing of five other units. This brings the total number of sealed units to 12, according to Taman Manggis PPR residents' association chairman Pannir Selvam. Pannir said residents received notices last November and were informed that action would be taken this month, but claimed some were not given adequate notice before their units were sealed.

items.title: Manila defence boss slams 'bullying' China after note at forum
items.summary: SEOUL: The Philippine defence chief has accused Beijing of "bullying", alleging he was handed a Chinese note at an international forum that asserted China's expansive claims over contested waters. "China's position on the South China Sea arbitration is clear, consistent, and firm.... The arbitration violates fundamental principles of international law," he said, reading from the note.

items.title: King's power to grant pardons must not be questioned - Umno
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno today criticised Pakatan Harapan (PH) for allegedly questioning the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's constitutional power to grant pardons. Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the power was clearly provided for under Article 42(1) of the Federal Constitution and should not be questioned by any party. MORE TO COME © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Cabinet expresses condolences to families of five killed in Sarawak FDS helicopter crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Cabinet today expressed its condolences to the families of the five victims who died in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak, yesterday. Unity government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and all ministers offered their sympathies and condolences at the weekly Cabinet meeting today. Fahmi, who is also the communications minister, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad had earlier announced the identities of all five victims.

items.title: Malaysian woman held at Delhi airport with 15kg cannabis worth RM2.2m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — A Malaysian woman was arrested by Indian authorities after she was caught attempting to smuggle 15 kilogrammes of cannabis, valued at approximately 52.5 million rupees (RM2.2 million), at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Sept 4. Delhi Customs (Airport & General) in a statement on X said the passenger, who arrived from Kuala Lumpur on flight OD-205, was intercepted at Terminal 3 based on profile-based targeting. An examination of her trolley bag led to the discovery of 30 polythene pouches containing suspected ganja (cannabis) weighing 15,015.5 grammes (net weight)," the department said.

items.title: Indonesian wildfire emissions surge to world's highest, data shows
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia is facing a surge in emissions from wildfires burning through parched stretches of forest and peatland on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra, with carbon dioxide readings currently the highest in the world, data showed on Wednesday. Fire emissions from Indonesia from September 1 to Sept 7 reached 19.7 million metric tonnes, overtaking Russia this week and making up more than a third of the global total, according to Fire Emissions Watch, a portal developed by the European Union's Copernicus climate monitoring service. From Sept 1 to Sept 7, fire emission intensity exceeded 1,500 kg/sq km, more than 10 times the Russian level, with the highest concentrations in Kalimantan in Indonesia's part of Borneo and eastern parts of Sumatra, Copernicus data showed on Wednesday.

items.title: [UPDATED] Azeez chose to wear lockup attire, handcuffs in court, says MACC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim chose to appear in court wearing a police lockup uniform and handcuffs despite being advised that he did not have to do so, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said. In a statement today, the anti-graft agency said Azeez's appearance in the purple police lockup attire and handcuffs when he was brought to the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to face charges was entirely at his own request. MACC said that before he was taken to court, its officers, accompanying police personnel and Azeez's lawyer had advised him to change into ordinary clothes.

items.title: Man, 5 juveniles charged over rape, gang rape of 15-year-old girl
items.summary: KANGAR: A man and five minors were charged separately in the Sessions Court and Magistrate's Court here today over the rape and gang rape of a 15-year-old girl last July. The accused was charged under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, which upon conviction carries a maximum sentence of 20 years' imprisonment and caning. The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutor Mohd Alif Farhan Hassan, while the accused was represented by lawyers Mohamad Alif Farhan Mohamad Supian and Zuhair Ahmad Zakuan.

items.title: Malicious prosecution: Shahrir's suit against three resolved, Thomas pending
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The civil suit filed by Tan Sri Shahrir Samad against former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Latheefa Koya, the commission and the Government of Malaysia over alleged malicious prosecution has been amicably resolved at the High Court here. However, the suit against former Attorney General Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, the first defendant, remains pending, with the court fixing Oct 16 to hear Shahrir's application for leave to discontinue the action against him. Shahrir and Thomas were present in court.

items.title: Businessman sentenced to 30 years’ jail, 24 strokes for trafficking more than 77kg of meth
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 9 — A businessman was sentenced to 30 years in prison and 24 strokes of the cane by the High Court here today after being found guilty of two counts of trafficking more than 77 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine five years ago. The court sentenced him to 30 years in prison and 12 strokes of the cane for the first and second counts respectively. According to the first charge, Liew is accused of distributing 74,477.8 grammes (74.48 kg) of methamphetamine, at the Gopeng Toll Plaza, towards the entrance to the highway before the toll payment counter, in the Kampar district at about 7.30 pm, June 23, 2021.

items.title: Eleven men, including college student, claim trial to armed rioting charge outside Air Itam school
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 9 — Eleven men, including a college student, reportedly pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court here today to a charge of rioting while armed with objects that could be used as weapons. The accused were named as Mohamad Nun Mohamad Jupri, 34; V. Rathakisnan, 22; Soman Sri Mahen Deren, 19; Muhammad Haikal Mohammad Rafiq, 19; Chad Sebastian George Albert, 19; Elijah Yong, 19; Cheow Junnuo, 24; Tony Yen Chun Yun, 19; R. Divagar, 20; Muhammad Amirul Hafiz Abdullah, 21; and Ng Chern Yeow, 24. Police previously detained 23 people to assist in investigations into the armed riot.

items.title: Six civil servants, five agents remanded over alleged falsified documents for illegal vehicle ownership transfers
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 9 — Eleven individuals, including six civil servants and five agents, have been remanded for six days to assist investigations into the alleged submission of falsified documents to facilitate illegal vehicle ownership transfers involving 16 registration numbers. Magistrate Norizan Riduan allowed the remand application, which runs from today until Sept 14, at the Magistrate’s Court here today. “Initial investigations found that the alleged offence took place in 2025, with the agents suspected of conspiring with civil servants to submit falsified documents to enable vehicle ownership transfers to be carried out illegally,” the source said.

items.title: Azeez posts RM450,000 bail after being charged with using position to secure chairmanship
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim emerged from the lock-up in purple remand attire and handcuffs to facilitate the RM450,000 bail process after claiming trial to using his position to secure a lucrative company chairmanship. Earlier, Azeez claimed trial to using his position 12 years ago to secure the post of chairman of Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, which carried an annual remuneration of RM690,000. He allegedly instructed TH chief executive officer Tan Sri Ismee Ismail to nominate him as TH's representative in Putrajaya Perdana Bhd.

items.title: Ex-KPTM administrator charged with 6 offences involving female students
items.summary: IPOH: A former Kolej Poly-Tech Mara (KPTM) administrator here was charged with six offences involving alleged use of criminal force against two female students and obscene words against four others. In the first courtroom, Roykarnaen was charged with intentionally using criminal force against a 19-year-old female student with the intention of outraging her modesty by pulling her arm towards her shoulder, placing his hand on her waist and kissing her forehead. Deputy Public Prosecutor Muhammad Zulqarnain Wan Asmira prosecuted, while lawyer Aiman Rusli represented the accused.

items.title: Capital A's Teleport 1H revenue jumps 35pct on e-commerce demand
items.summary: Profit after tax stood at US$3.1 million, with the second quarter marking Teleport's fourth consecutive profitable quarter. In Southeast Asia, its volume grew 34 per cent in 1H26, nearly three times the regional market growth of 12 per cent. Across Asia Pacific, Teleport's revenue increased 26 per cent and volume rose 12 per cent, compared with declines of three per cent in revenue and five per cent in volume for the wider Asia Pacific air cargo market.

items.title: [UPDATED] Malaysia ready to send assets to fight Indonesia fires, awaits Indonesia's approval
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia is ready to send assets to help Indonesia tackle forest fires contributing to the haze, pending confirmation and approval. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and the Foreign Ministry had informed the cabinet that Malaysia had prepared a list of assets to assist Indonesia. KW: NST, Malaysia news, Malaysia, Indonesia, haze, forest fires, Nadma, Fahmi Fadzil, Malaysia Day, Sarawak, Kuching, transboundary haze, Anwar Ibrahim © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Four killed after car carrying three foreign nationals collides with lorry in Telupid
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 9 — Four people were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a lorry in Kampung Gambaron, Telupid, about 230 kilometres from here, this morning. The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said it received an emergency call on the crash involving two vehicles travelling in opposite directions at 7.28 am. “Four victims were in the car and were extricated by firefighters, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Civil Defence Force before medical personnel from the Health Ministry (MOH) confirmed that they died at the scene,” it said in a statement today.

items.title: Zara inquest: Psychiatrist explains assessment of diary entries, informants
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Consultant forensic psychiatrist Dr Chua Sze Hung told the Coroner's Court today that he had considered the positive aspects of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir's diaries in his assessment. So yes, I have taken these factors into consideration," said Dr Chua. The Coroner then questioned whether the positive aspects were reflected in Dr Chua's report.

items.title: 'Where's daddy?': Pilot's daughter longs for father killed in heli crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "Mommy, daddy will be back tomorrow, right? Sofia misses daddy. "Sofia, mommy and daddy love Sofia.

items.title: Guan Eng submits ‘Malaysia Agenda 12’ package to Anwar, proposes RM25b in interest-free MSME loans
items.summary: In a hand-delivered letter yesterday, the DAP adviser proposed RM25 billion in interest-free and collateral-free loans for 500,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), alongside a one-year interest moratorium on their existing bank loans. “The banking industry can afford to bear the cost of the interest moratorium on existing MSME loans for one year,” he said. Lim estimated that financing the interest-free loans would cost RM1 billion annually at a 4 per cent interest rate, citing the banking industry’s RM54.8 billion profit before tax in 2025 — a 13.5 per cent increase from 2024.

items.title: Rapid KL to replace Kelana Jaya line track in stages from Sunday
items.summary: According to the statement, stations involved in the track replacement work will begin operating at 9.30 am compared to the usual 6 am, while stations not involved will operate as usual according to schedule. The track replacement work involves Gombak and Taman Melati stations on Sept 13, 20 and 27, followed by the second phase for Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum stations (Nov 15, 22 and 29), as well as the third phase covering Dato' Keramat, Jelatek and Setiawangsa stations (Jan 10, 17 and 24, 2027). Meanwhile, the sixth phase involves Taman Jaya, Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum stations on 11, 18 and 25 July 2027, while the final phase involves Gombak and Taman Melati stations on 12, 19 and 26 Sept 2027.

items.title: [UPDATED] Dengue cases surge 66pct, deaths nearly double
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Dengue cases have risen by 66 per cent as of epidemiological week 35 this year compared with the same period in 2025. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said 65,979 cases had been recorded this year, compared with 39,616 cases during the same period last year. Meanwhile, Fahmi said, the Housing and Local Government Ministry would hold large-scale gotong-royong programmes, including in areas identified as red zones or where outbreaks had occurred.

items.title: Another Malaysian pilot arrested over Jakarta drug syndicate probe, says Bukit Aman
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR, Sept 9 — Another local pilot has been arrested to assist in investigations in connection with the detention of a Malaysion co-pilot in Jakarta in July for suspected involvement in an international drug trafficking syndicate. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the Malaysian man, in his 30s, was arrested on Monday (Sept 7) in the Klang Valley. “Police seized various types of drugs, including 61.26kg of methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) liquid, ecstasy pills (0.79kg), cannabis flower (6.09kg), Erimin 5 pills (3.80kg), cannabis (11.13kg), methamphetamine (3.25kg), cannabis-laced biscuits (870 grammes), ketamine (490 grammes) and MDMA powder (480 grammes).

items.title: Sarawak govt to channel RM100,000 to each family of FDS helicopter crash victims
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 9 — The Sarawak State Government will channel a contribution of RM100,000 to each family of personnel involved in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, yesterday. In a statement on social media by the Sarawak Public Communications Unit (UKAS), the state government announced it will also fully cover the education fees of the victims’ children who are still in school through the Sarawak Foundation. “Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg agreed that the assistance be channelled as a sign of the Sarawak State Government’s concern to help ease the burden of the families and the next of kin involved.

items.title: [UPDATED] Cabinet extends condolences to families of Long Lellang helicopter crash victims
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has extended its condolences to the families of five people killed in yesterday's Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) was investigating the incident and would submit its findings to the Cabinet. In the incident yesterday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport), Ulu Baram.

items.title: Hadi calls for abolition of ‘colonial laws’ to make Syariah rule supreme in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has called for the abolition of laws he described as colonial legacies, alleging that these were obstacles to the unfettered implementation of Syariah law in Malaysia. In the statement, titled “Merdeka: Hapus Undang-Undang Penjajah Yang Sekat Pelaksanaan Islam” (”Independence: Abolish Colonial Laws That Obstruct the Implementation of Islam”), the Marang MP argued that true independence cannot be realised while laws inherited from British rule continue to limit Islam’s position above man-made legislation. “Colonial-legacy laws must be abolished to ensure the true meaning of independence can be fully realised,” Hadi said in the statement.

items.title: Woman seeks help to find husband missing since Sept 6
items.summary: KULAI: A woman is desperately seeking help to locate her husband, who has been uncontactable since Sept 6, leaving their children pining for their father. Meanwhile, district police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee confirmed that a police report was lodged on Sept 7. He said Bandar Tenggara police were investigating the missing person report.

items.title: Mikro MSC to acquire cable manufacturer Broadguard for RM30mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mikro MSC Bhd is acquiring Broadguard Sdn Bhd for RM30 million to expand its business into the wholesale and distribution of cables and related products used in security and surveillance systems. Sie will receive RM24 million worth of shares, while Wong will receive RM6 million worth. Its revenue rose to RM17.62 million in the financial year ended April 30, 2026 (FY26) from RM14.80 million a year earlier, while profit after tax increased to RM2.15 million from RM1.39 million.

items.title: Pas backs political funding bill in principle, seeks more details
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas supports the proposed Political Financing Bill in principle, saying it is necessary to uphold the democratic system and safeguard the rights of political parties. Its deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man, however, said Pas needed more details on the proposed bill before making a final decision on its position. "Basically, we agree that political financing should be implemented to ensure the democratic system is respected and the rights of every political party are protected.

items.title: TNB Genco continues investing in fleet reliability, renewables and storage pipeline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: TNB Power Generation Sdn Bhd (TNB Genco) continues to invest in the reliability of its existing generation fleet while advancing its renewable and storage pipeline, including a hybrid hydro-floating solar project combining 595 megawatts (MW) of floating solar with 1,190 megawatt-hours (MWh) of battery storage, targeted for completion in 2028. "As Malaysia's largest power producer, TNB Genco plays a central role in shaping the country's energy mix," said TNB Genco's managing director Datuk Shahrir Abdul Latiff. The approach reflects TNB's broader commitment to advancing Malaysia's energy transition while safeguarding the reliability the nation depends on.

items.title: Zara's diaries 'most critical, uncontaminated premortem data', court told
items.summary: Consultant forensic psychiatrist Dr Chua Sze Hung said this while testifying before coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan. During examination-in-chief, Dr Chua was asked about consultant psychiatrist Dr Simon Wong devoting a section of his report to a "Psychiatric Assessment of the Mother", based on an interview on Jan 5 this year, almost six months after Zara's death. Asked whether an assessment of a surviving parent was a proper substitute for assessing the deceased adolescent's mental state, Dr Chua replied: "No."

items.title: Negeri Sembilan royal dispute: Rembau Undang says MB sign-off cannot validate flawed proclamation
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — Rembau Undang Dato’ Sedia Raja Haji Hassan bin Haji Ab. Hamid today said the Menteri Besar’s signature could not validate a proclamation concerning the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan if the process leading to it was flawed. In a statement, Hassan said the main question was not whether the proclamation existed or how many people had signed it, but whether the process complied with the Negeri Sembilan Constitution and Adat Perpatih.

items.title: Umno strengthens digital machinery with AIRA ahead of GE16
items.summary: Umno Information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said AIRA had already been used during the Sabah and Negri Sembilan elections to help candidates and the public obtain information and clarification about issues and candidates. Also present were Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail, secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan. The Pengerang member of parliament said AIRA, or Artificial Intelligence Rakyat Assistant, was developed by Umno's Information Department in collaboration with the Umno Patriotic School.

items.title: Six civil servants among 11 remanded over vehicle document falsification
items.summary: IPOH: Eleven people, including six civil servants, have been remanded to assist investigations into an alleged syndicate involved in submitting falsified documents for vehicle ownership transfers. Norizan allowed the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC)'s application to remand the suspects from today until Monday. A source said the suspects had conspired to submit falsified documents to the RTD for vehicle ownership transfers involving 16 registration numbers.

items.title: Malaysian woman nabbed at Delhi airport with RM2.24mil worth of ganja
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian woman was arrested at Indira Gandhi International Airport in India on Friday after she was caught with more than 15kg of ganja worth 52.5 million rupees, or about RM2.24 million. The woman was detained while the drugs were seized under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act. It remains unknown whether the woman was paid to carry the drugs.

items.title: Protesters urge South Korea to stay out of Iran war
items.summary: SEOUL: Dozens of South Koreans urged their government on Wednesday not to deploy troops to the strategic Strait of Hormuz, slamming what they called Washington's "illegal war." US President Donald Trump has pressured ally South Korea to help in the Middle East war, which has seen Iran take a stranglehold on the strait key to global oil supplies. "As Iran has said, the deployment of our troops to the region would amount to direct participation in an illegal war," he said.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB says he signed proclamation on Tuanku Muhriz under duress, files police report
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today confirmed that he signed a proclamation concerning the position of Tuanku Muhriz ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir as the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, but said he had done so unwillingly and under duress. “The state government maintains that the Instrument did not comply with the processes and procedures stipulated under Article 10 of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959,” he said. Ismail said the state executive council also discussed establishing a reconciliation committee during its meeting yesterday.

items.title: Former childcare assistant charged with abusing two-year-old boy at Mentakab centre
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Sept 9 — A former childcare assistant was charged at the Sessions Court here today with abusing a two-year-old boy at a childcare centre in Mentakab last month. According to the charge, she allegedly abused the child in a manner that could have caused emotional injury at a childcare centre in Taman Keramat Indah, Mentakab, at about 9.45am on Aug 11. Judge Jamaludin allowed bail at RM5,000 with one surety and set Oct 14 for mention.

items.title: Police uncover RM2.4b drug operation in Puncak Alam, seize 13.17 tonnes in biggest haul this year
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR, Sept 9 — Police have crippled a drug processing and distribution syndicate and uncovered a drug laboratory in Puncak Alam here through Op Eumenes conducted in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur, with the total drugs seized estimated to be worth RM2.4 billion on Aug 15. Elaborating, Hussein said the total value of the drugs seized was estimated at RM2.4 billion, making it the biggest drug seizure believed to have been recorded this year. Meanwhile, he said police believed the syndicate leader was an individual who was shot dead in a previous raid in Seremban.

items.title: Perak rejects claim Taiping Hospital has no house officers, says 93 currently undergoing training
items.summary: Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the hospital currently has 93 house officers out of 231 training slots allocated, giving it a 40.3 per cent placement rate. Sivanesan said he had met the Taiping Hospital director and obtained clarification on the hospital’s current staffing situation. “The optimum requirement for medical officers at Hospital Taiping is estimated at 273,” he said.

items.title: Report: Najib’s clemency bid expected to be discussed by Pardons Board this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application for clemency when it meets this week, according to sources cited by Free Malaysia Today (FMT). FMT reported that sources familiar with the matter said Najib’s application was expected to be among the issues raised at the board’s meeting, although it remained unclear whether the meeting would result in a decision or merely a discussion. A separate source told the online news portal that Najib could potentially be allowed to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, although it was unclear whether the option would be considered at the meeting.

items.title: King, Queen extend condolences to families of Sarawak helicopter crash victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia have expressed their condolences to the families of the pilot and Ministry of Health (MOH) personnel who died in a helicopter crash in Sarawak, yesterday. Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) in a statement announced that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals including the pilot crashed near the Long Lellang Short Runway Airport (STOLport), Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching, Sarawak. CAAM received information about the incident involving the helicopter from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Rescue teams begin evacuation of Long Lellang helicopter crash victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Rescue teams are working to evacuate victims of the helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, with the operation beginning at 7.30 am today, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said. He said the operation was being carried out by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM). Also present were Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab and Deputy Health director-general (Public Health) Dr Ismuni Bohari.

items.title: Rapid KL to begin Kelana Jaya Line track replacement works on Sept 13
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Rapid KL will begin phased track replacement works on the Kelana Jaya Line from Sunday, with affected stations starting services at 9.30am on designated Sundays instead of the usual 6am. The affected stations and dates are: Phase 1: Sept 13, 20 and 27, 2026 — Taman Melati and Gombak Phase 2: Nov 15, 22 and 29, 2026 — Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum Phase 3: Jan 10, 17 and 24, 2027 — Dato’ Keramat, Jelatek and Setiawangsa Phase 4: March 14, 21 and 28, 2027 — Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum Phase 5: May 9, 16 and 23, 2027 — Masjid Jamek, Dang Wangi, Kampung Baru, KLCC and Ampang Park Phase 6: July 11, 18 and 25, 2027 — Taman Jaya, Universiti, Kerinchi and Abdullah Hukum Phase 7: Sept 12, 19 and 26, 2027 — Taman Melati and Gombak Rapid KL said trains at stations not affected by the track replacement works would operate as usual according to their daily operating schedules. Free shuttle buses Rapid KL will provide free shuttle buses connecting the affected stations throughout the track replacement works to help passengers continue their journeys.

items.title: Anwar: Govt to provide assistance, support to families of five killed in Sarawak helicopter crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — The government will provide all necessary assistance and support to the families of the five victims killed in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak. Anwar said he was deeply saddened by the crash involving a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter carrying four Health Ministry (MOH) personnel and a pilot yesterday afternoon. Yesterday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said that a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport (STOLport) in Ulu Baram, about 929 kilometres from Kuching.

items.title: Pilot killed in Sarawak helicopter crash had video call with mother for more than an hour before tragedy, says father
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — A video call lasting more than an hour with his mother on the night before the incident turned out to be the final moment for the family of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 31, who was involved in a helicopter crash in Sarawak yesterday. His father, Bee Sham Ahmad, 59, said his fourth child of 12 siblings had a lengthy video call with his mother, Zaiton Muda, 59, on the night before the crash. “We only learned the sad news from my eighth child, who informed us that his brother had been involved in the crash yesterday afternoon,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.

items.title: Perak steps up preparations for Super El Nino expected to last until early 2027
items.summary: He said the phenomenon was expected to persist until early 2027, prompting the state government to continuously strengthen its preparedness measures. On public health, Saarani said the Perak Health Department (JKN Perak) was guided by the Health Ministry’s 2021 Action Plan for Managing Health Risks from Heatwaves. “This also includes ensuring sufficient supplies of critical medicines,” he said.

items.title: Former TH chairman Abdul Azeez charged with abuse of power involving RM190m investment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim was charged today with receiving gratification by using his position to influence a decision to invest RM190 million in a company in which he is accused of having an interest. Azeez was alleged to have directed then TH chief executive officer Tan Sri Ismi Ismail to nominate him as a board member of Perdana Putra Berhad, a subsidiary, and using his position to influence TH’s board members to invest in the said company. Deputy public prosecutor Datuk Ahmad Akram Gharib, leading the prosecution, initially asked for bail to be set at RM1 million with additional terms.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan royal dispute: Sungei Ujong Undang says Tuanku Muhriz removal bid invalid despite purported MB sign-off
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 9 — Sungei Ujong Undang Dato’ Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari Meor Ngah today said a declaration purportedly signed by the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar concerning the removal of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, was invalid and could not take effect. In a statement, Muhammad Faris maintained that the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) had ruled at an earlier sitting that the April 19 declaration concerning Tuanku Muhriz had no legal effect because it did not meet the requirements of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution. The statement followed a claim by another group of traditional leaders that Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had signed the proclamation at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson on August 3, completing the document first issued on April 19.

items.title: No hazardous API readings nationwide, but Serian records very unhealthy level
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — No area nationwide recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at hazardous levels due to the haze as of 9 am this morning. However, the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal this morning showed that only Serian in Sarawak recorded a very unhealthy API of 214. Meanwhile, 10 areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy readings, namely Samarahan and Kuching with 185 each, Sarikei (174), Sri Aman (173), Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (171), Samalaju (169), Mukah (156), Bintulu (155), Miri (150) and Sibu (102).

items.title: Gombak Setia assemblyman Hilman acquitted of making TikTok statement capable of causing public alarm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Gombak Setia assemblyman Muhammad Hilman Idham was acquitted and discharged by the Magistrate’s Court here today of a charge of making a statement on TikTok that allegedly could cause public alarm. Magistrate Nurul Izzah Hasan Basri found that the prosecution had failed to establish the essential elements of the charge under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code. “In conclusion, the prosecution has failed to establish a prima facie case against the accused at the close of the prosecution’s case.

items.title: Kelantan MB: Doctor killed in Sarawak helicopter crash dedicated to serving rural communities
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 9 — Kelantan has lost a Kota Bharu-born, the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, who passed away while carrying out her mission through the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) for the rural communities of Sarawak. Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud said the official confirmation of the deceased’s passing was heartbreaking when she was serving to bring treatment and hope to those in need. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad was reported to have said that the helicopter that departed from Miri was operated by a pilot and carried a medical officer, an assistant medical officer (PPP) and two nurses who were carrying out official duties.

items.title: Those convicted of corruption should serve full court sentences, Pakatan says ahead of Najib pardon bid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has maintained that individuals convicted of corruption or abuse of power, particularly in high-profile cases, should serve the full sentences imposed by the courts. PH said previous high-profile corruption cases had damaged Malaysia’s international reputation, while recent efforts had helped rebuild confidence in the country’s institutions and governance. The statement came ahead of a reported Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting scheduled for Friday.

items.title: Former TH chair Abdul Azeez faces police remand proceedings, corruption charge today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim was brought to the magistrate’s court for a remand hearing before facing a corruption charge today. Datuk Abu Bakar Isa Ramat, Azeez’s lawyer, said the Umno leader was arrested by the Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department yesterday afternoon before being taken to the Dang Wangi police station. Azeez, a member of Umno’s supreme council, had already been detained by the Malaysian Anti Corruption Commission for seven days, which ends today.
